scope: Logical data model and reversible local-storage operations plan only. No persistence technology, first platform, product policy, schema migration, production operation, or release is approved or implemented.

dependencyEvidence.persistenceSelection: undecided between an embedded transactional database and atomic local manifest files
dependencyEvidence.sharedBusinessRuleBoundary: The shared download domain service exclusively validates transitions and policies. The repository persists accepted domain snapshots and events but does not infer, authorize, or redefine state transitions.

aggregates.name: download
aggregates.purpose: Durable recovery snapshot owned by the shared download domain

fields.name: sourceUrl
constraints: credentials must not be embedded or persisted

fields.name: partialPath
constraints: must not equal a finalized completed artifact

fields.name: receivedBytes
constraints: must not exceed expectedBytes when known

fields.name: remoteIdentity
constraints: store a URL hash rather than redirect history

fields.name: failure
constraints: no raw credentials, headers, or sensitive URL query values

invariants: Only the shared domain service may create a new persisted state or increment revision.
A completed record requires successful finalization, no partialPath, and integrity evidence when an expected digest exists.
A resumable record requires a partialPath, receivedBytes greater than zero, and remote identity evidence validated again at runtime.
Persistence success is acknowledged only after the complete snapshot is durably committed.
Unknown states, schema versions, or stale revisions fail closed without overwriting the last valid snapshot.

deliberatelyExcluded: Passwords, cookies, authorization headers, and browser credentials
Transfer chunks or downloaded content inside the metadata store

storageContract.metadata: Use one application-owned local store per operating-system user profile. The concrete engine remains unselected until ADR-02 is approved.
storageContract.content: Write bytes to an application-recognizable partial file on the destination filesystem, flush according to the approved durability budget, then finalize with the platform adapter's verified atomic operation where supported.
storageContract.atomicUnit: An accepted domain snapshot, its revision, and schema metadata must commit together. File finalization and the completed snapshot require a recoverable two-phase protocol because they cross database and filesystem boundaries.
completionProtocol: Domain marks the transfer finalizing without exposing completed.
Storage flushes and closes the partial file and performs required integrity verification.
Platform adapter atomically moves or replaces according to the approved destination-conflict policy.
Repository persists the completed snapshot and clears partialPath.
Startup reconciliation repairs a crash between finalization and metadata commit by checking both paths and integrity evidence; it never assumes completion from file presence alone.
startupRecovery: Open the store read-only first and validate format, schema version, and integrity before any migration.
Convert snapshots left in active or finalizing to interrupted unless reconciliation proves finalized content and the domain accepts completion.
Treat missing, shortened, or mismatched partial files as a recoverable failure; never advance receivedBytes from metadata alone.
Quarantine corrupt metadata and offer restore or explicit reset; do not silently discard download history.
security: Use operating-system user-only permissions for metadata, backups, and partial files where the destination permits.
Redact sensitive URL components and safe failure messages before logs or diagnostics.
If authenticated downloads enter approved scope, credentials require an operating-system credential store and only an opaque reference may appear in metadata.
Backups inherit the same sensitivity and access controls as the live metadata store.

migrationPlan.strategy: Versioned, forward-only expand-migrate-contract steps with a pre-migration backup and an application compatibility window; every release must declare minimumReadableSchema and maximumWritableSchema.
steps: Acquire the single-writer lock and stop transfer mutations.
Validate store integrity, free-space headroom, and supported source schema.
Create and verify a point-in-time local backup without modifying the source.
Apply an idempotent expand step; preserve unknown fields when the selected format supports it.
Migrate records in bounded transactions or via write-new-then-atomic-swap for manifest storage.
Validate record counts, identifiers, state values, revisions, byte bounds, and completed/partial invariants.
Record schema metadata and reopen through the repository contract before deleting any obsolete representation.
Retain the pre-migration backup through the approved rollback window.
migrationPlan.rollback: Before an irreversible contract step, rollback means stop the new application, preserve the failed store for diagnosis, restore the verified pre-migration backup atomically, and run the older compatible application. Down-migrations that could discard data are prohibited.
migrationPlan.failureBehavior: Any validation or write failure leaves the original store or verified backup intact, exits read-only or unavailable with an actionable error, and performs no automatic destructive reset.
requiredMigrationTests: Empty store and representative vN store upgrade
Upgrade with every valid download state
Crash or process termination at each migration phase
Insufficient disk space before and during copy
Corrupt source store and corrupt backup detection
Old-application rollback using the retained backup
Paths, timestamps, large byte counters, and redacted sensitive URL fixtures across each approved platform

backupRestorePlan.scope: Local metadata and schema metadata; downloaded and partial content remain filesystem assets and are not duplicated by metadata backup.
backupRestorePlan.trigger: Create a backup before every schema migration and before any operator-approved repair. Scheduled user backups are a product decision and are not claimed.
backupRestorePlan.consistency: Use the selected engine's consistent snapshot facility or close the writer and copy to a temporary sibling before atomic rename.
verification: Validate store checksum or engine integrity check
Validate schema compatibility and logical invariants
Record creation time, schema version, size, and checksum without sensitive contents
restore: Stop writers and preserve the current store under a timestamped recovery name.
Verify backup checksum, format, schema compatibility, and free space.
Restore to a temporary sibling, open and validate it, then atomically swap where the platform supports it.
Run startup reconciliation against partial and finalized files before enabling commands.
Retain the displaced store until the restored application passes the recovery smoke test.
backupRestorePlan.retention: Retention count and duration require product/privacy approval. Until approved, pre-migration backups must not be automatically deleted by implementation.

recoveryObjectives.rpo: undecided; pre-migration state is the minimum guaranteed recovery point
recoveryObjectives.rto: undecided; measure against the largest supported metadata store on each approved platform

indexPlan.principle: Add indexes only for measured repository queries after a concrete engine is selected; indexes are rebuildable derivatives, not backup data.

candidateAccessPaths.justification: Bounds restart scan when history is retained
Stable keyset pagination without offset drift

constraints: Do not index sourceUrl, destination, failure message, or credential references unless a separately reviewed feature requires it.
Do not add indexes until query plans and write amplification are measured.
Index creation must be interruptible or use the migration backup-and-swap procedure.

drivers: partial and completed content on destination volumes
capacityPlan.metadataBudgetFormula: requiredMetadataBytes = liveStoreBytes + max(liveStoreBytes, migrationGrowthBytes) + retainedBackupBytes + safetyMarginBytes
guardrails: Measure serialized record size and store/index amplification with representative URLs, paths, failures, and large counters before setting limits.
Preflight free space before transfer, migration, backup, restore, and non-atomic finalization; recheck during long operations.
Use unsigned 64-bit semantics with checked arithmetic for byte counts and capacity calculations.
Bound retained history and backup policy only after product and privacy approval; warn before limits are reached and never silently delete active or partial work.
Benchmark startup recovery and migration at the approved maximum record count on Windows, macOS, and Linux filesystems in scope.

repositoryTests: Repository contract tests must run against every selected storage adapter
Domain-state persistence tests must drive commands through the shared domain service, not direct record mutation
Property tests must cover stale revisions, invalid states, byte overflow, partial/completed invariants, and unknown schema versions
integrationScenarios: process termination at every completion-protocol step
server with invalid or absent range support
backup, restore, migration, and rollback on each approved platform

traceability.limitation: Persistence selection and platform foundation remain unapproved.
Supported operating systems, versions, and filesystems remain undecided.
Final capability dispositions require the human product decision.
Independent disposition is reserved for ENG-15.

implementationNotes: No database, migration, application code, infrastructure, credentials, deployment, or production data were touched.
No concrete schema was created because ADR-02 explicitly leaves persistence technology undecided; this logical contract is designed to map to either approved option.
Storage adapters persist domain outputs and recovery facts only. They must never duplicate or decide download business rules.
User-visible recovery and error behavior requires real desktop or equivalent integration runtime evidence after an application exists.
knownRisks: The human product owner has not approved the first platform, bounded MVP, cancellation behavior, destination-conflict policy, or history retention.
Persistence technology is undecided, so engine-specific transaction, locking, integrity-check, and migration behavior remains unverified.
Database metadata and filesystem content cannot share one transaction; crash-safe completion and reconciliation need adversarial integration tests.
Partial files may live on filesystems without atomic rename, durable flush, or reliable free-space reporting; supported filesystems must be bounded.
Sensitive URLs can leak through metadata, backups, diagnostics, or error strings without explicit redaction tests.
Capacity limits, RPO, RTO, and retention are unresolved and require measured workloads plus product/privacy approval.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
